newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes rate under pressure from soft peso.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes rate under pressure from soft peso.

text.p: MEXICO CITY, March 11 - Mexican overnight Cetes rates opened up 85 basis points at 23.00 percent in response to early pressure on the peso, traders said.

"Rates are under pressure above all due to the peso. Furthermore, Banco de Mexico participating at longer maturities yesterday has made waves and some dealers are taking advantage of that to push rates up," a trader said.
Benchmark 48-hour peso contracts were 1.9 centavos weaker in early trade at 7.9790/7.9830 per dollar.
The central bank drained liquidity on Monday at up to 43 days, compared with a usual maximum maturity of 28 days.
"It's auction day, which lends itself to speculation," the trader added.
Banco de Mexico will hold its weekly auction of government securities later in the day.

Traders said they expected rates on bellwether 28-day Cetes to increase by 85 basis points, from last week's rate of 21.16 percent, if current pressure on the peso persisted. Overnight rates on bank paper were meanwhile up 55 basis points at 24.65 percent.
Dealers said short-term primary rates were also under pressure from a possible announcement of increased U.S. interest rates at the March 25 Federal Open Market Committee meeting.
Liquidity of 267 million pesos was scheduled to return to the system from prior central bank participation
